lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Make the profile link a direct, working link.
items.because: It should lead to your professional profile.

items.says: Check that the email and phone are appropriate for applications.
Verify the MBA dates and degree status for this version of the résumé.
items.because: A completed MBA should not appear to be in progress.

items.says: Put the Harbor Payments internship above Crestline Logistics.
items.because: The internship ended in 2024, so the current order makes the reverse-chronological timeline harder to follow.

items.says: Make the career transition and product target clear around the current mechanic role.
items.because: Recruiters may be unsure why you are applying for product roles.

items.says: Emphasize the mechanic role’s aspects most relevant to the target role.
items.because: The newest job is unrelated to product management.

items.says: Clarify how “under 5 days per job” was measured and whether it was typical or a target.
items.because: That would make the achievement easier to interpret.

items.says: Specify whether the hydraulic-systems responsibility covered all relevant systems or a subset.
items.because: The bullet reads more like a duty than a distinctive achievement.

items.says: Check whether “rebuilt” accurately describes the scorecard work.
items.because: It may suggest reconstruction rather than improvement.

items.says: Clarify how the scorecards and contract renegotiations contributed to fewer late deliveries.
items.because: The contribution needs to be credible and clear.

items.says: Remove the first-person “my.”
items.because: It disrupts the résumé’s voice.

items.says: Clarify whether you trained the 45 pickers or coordinated their training.
Make the relationship between the slotting redesign and error reduction explicit.
Define the forecast-error measure and how it was calculated.
items.because: “Forecast error” can be defined in different ways.

items.says: Separate or prioritize the many contributions in the rollout bullet.
items.because: The most important work gets lost in a long list.

items.says: Explain the basis for the 1,800-driver-hour figure.
items.because: It gets lost among the listed contributions.

items.says: Clarify whether the 2,300 merchants were in the pilot or the eligible population.
items.because: Recruiters need to judge the result’s scale and reliability.

items.says: State the measurement period for the onboarding result.
items.because: Recruiters need to judge the result’s scale and reliability.

items.says: Describe the conversion change as a five-percentage-point lift.
items.because: The change from 61% to 66% may otherwise be interpreted imprecisely.

items.says: Distinguish the test result from the later rollout.
items.because: The bullet does not say whether the lift persisted after launch.

items.says: Include test duration or statistical confidence if accurate and useful.
Add the decision or outcome supported by the RICE prioritization.
items.because: The bullet describes a method without showing its value.

items.says: Explain or validate support-ticket volume as the Reach measure.
items.because: It may be a proxy that readers familiar with RICE will question.

items.says: Reduce the overlap with the RICE bullet about setting the roadmap.
items.because: Both bullets concern setting the roadmap.

items.says: Make the research result clearer, including why the priority mattered or what happened next.
items.because: The bullet lists activities without showing the priority’s importance or subsequent outcome.

items.says: The conversion result repeats the preceding bullet.
items.because: The bullets do not clearly offer distinct evidence.

items.says: Clarify what “effect on merchants’ customers” means.
items.because: The metric is customer conversion, while the business impact may be on merchants.

items.says: Distinguish funding approval from an actual rollout.
items.because: Readers may assume the two additional regions were already live.

items.says: Clarify how the 9 tonnes were measured.
Define the period meant by “first year.”
Distinguish students reached at launch from active users.
items.because: Those are different measures.

items.says: The increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%, not 150%.
Clarify whether the interviews led specifically to pickup reminders.
Clarify whether the user increase was measured over a comparable period.
Moving from 75% to 95% is a 20-percentage-point increase, not a 20% increase.
State the period over which the fill rate was measured.
Distinguish modeled annual savings from savings actually realized.
items.because: Readers could mistake the estimate for a delivered result.

items.says: Show the basis or validation of the savings estimate if available.
Replace the passive construction to show your role.
items.because: The current wording hides your contribution.

items.says: Quantify how much the form was shortened or what improved.
items.because: “Shortened” does not convey either result.

items.says: Clarify how extensively front-desk staff adopted the changes.
The pilot approval duplicates the outcome in the savings bullet.
items.because: The bullets do not clearly show distinct contributions or outcomes.

items.says: Ensure the listed product skills are substantiated and relevant to target roles.
items.because: The list emphasizes methods but not the analytical or delivery skills suggested by the bullets.

items.says: List only tools you can use confidently and discuss from experience.
Specify the level and type of Excel work you have done.
items.because: “Excel” is broad.

items.says: Use consistent date formatting, punctuation, capitalization, and bullet style throughout.
Give every metric a clear unit, timeframe, and comparison point.
Make the product experience and intended direction apparent quickly.
items.because: The current mechanic role and the gap between Crestline and the internship may prompt questions.
